Without TOX the cells express lower PD-1, CD160, LAG3 and TIGIT, show improved function, generate more KLRG1+CD127- effectors, lose Eomes and nearly all TCF1 expression with a near absence of the TCF1+ subset, and their day-8 transcriptome shifts to an effector-like program with more than 3,100 differentially expressed genes, enriched for the effector signature and depleted of the exhausted-precursor signature. Partially TOX-deficient tumour-specific T cells control tumour growth significantly better than wild-type cells. The authors state that TOX is largely dispensable for effector and memory formation, but is critical for exhaustion and without TOX exhausted T cells do not form.
limitations: Mouse LCMV and ectopic tumour models with transgenic TCR cells; human exhaustion is addressed only by expression data elsewhere in the paper.
Conditional deletion is present before the response begins, so the experiment tests formation of the exhausted state and not maintenance of an established one.

TOX-deficient cells are not simply functional: they are short-lived in chronic infection and skew to a terminal effector phenotype, so loss of the exhaustion program is not equivalent to preserved immunity.
TOX is one transcription factor within a broader gene-regulatory program, and the calcineurin-NFAT2 input upstream of it is a separate arm.
Read in the Europe PMC full text with figure legends; Extended Data figures are cited by the authors but were not inspected.
studies.observable: Donor P14 cell numbers over time, KLRG1 and CD127 effector phenotype, PD-1, CD160, LAG3, TIGIT, 2B4 and TIM3 expression, cytokine function, TCF1, Eomes and T-bet expression, genome-wide transcriptional signatures, and tumour growth
studies.preparation: Naive TOX conditional-knockout P14 cells are mixed one to one with wild-type P14 cells and transferred into recipients, so both genotypes experience the same infection in the same animal. Chronic clone 13 and acute Armstrong infections are compared over more than 30 days; donor-cell number, Ki-67, inhibitory receptors, transcription factors and function are measured by flow cytometry, and sorted day-8 cells are profiled transcriptionally. A separate arm transfers tumour-specific T cells with conditional deletion of one Tox allele into an ectopic tumour model.

studies.finding: sgRNAs targeting Smo or the intraflagellar transport subunit Ift88 severely reduce ShhN-induced blasticidin resistance, paralleled by concordant changes in GLI1 expression and GLI3 processing, whereas Gli3 loss potentiates resistance and Sufu loss gives ligand-independent resistance. The authors describe the primary cilium as a surface-exposed microtubule-based compartment required for Hedgehog signaling output.
limitations: One fibroblast line and one pathway, read through an engineered antibiotic-resistance reporter at saturating ligand.
Knockouts act in growing populations; cilium loss in the validation knockouts is not quantified in the passages read.
Supplementary figures, including the immunoblots of pathway outputs, were not inspected.

studies.finding: The source reports whole-cell PROPS flashes with stable intracellular pH within its stated control precision, supporting transient depolarization. Respiration interruption and uncoupling replace blinking with sustained bright PROPS response; illumination changes blinking frequency and duration. The source separates voltage-sensitive and pH-sensitive signals. Membrane voltage alone is not a measured concentration gradient for every solute, a complete proton-motive-force budget or a globally constant cellular state.
limitations: Voltage is inferred from a fluorescent sensor and calibration, not direct bacterial voltage clamp. Exact SI controls and protocols remain unread.
PROPS is also pH-sensitive, making the separate pHluorin control essential. Reporter intensity is not directly the count or identity of an open channel.
Imaging light changes the behavior and its mechanism was unknown in the source. The reported maximal blinking frequency is not a universal physiological clock.
A neuronal Hodgkin-Huxley model does not validate this bacterial preparation; neither every transport process nor all biochemical equilibrium shifts were measured.
studies.observable: PROPS fluorescence transients, pH-sensitive control fluorescence and responses to respiratory/uncoupling perturbations.
studies.preparation: In the source PROPS-expressing E. coli preparation under an agarose pad and minimal medium, compare optical voltage responses with coexpressed cytoplasmic pHluorin and metabolic/illumination perturbations. studies.finding: Splenocytes from naive IL-15-/- mice show a severe reduction or absence of cells with an NK1.1+CD3- phenotype. Control splenocytes give low to weak spontaneous NK activity and strong activity after polyI:C, whereas splenocytes from IL-15-/- mice exhibit no demonstrable spontaneous or polyI:C-inducible NK activity against YAC-1 targets, while heterozygous cells are indistinguishable from wild type. Seven daily injections of human IL-15 give both control and IL-15-/- mice strong splenic NK activity and a more than twelvefold increase in absolute splenic NK cell number, with similar 1.5- to 2-fold increases in splenic cellularity in both groups and no effect on splenic B or CD4 T cell numbers. The authors conclude an obligate role for IL-15 in the development and functional maturation of NK cells, and note that the defect is reversible.
limitations: One mouse knockout line maintained under specific-pathogen-free conditions; germline deletion removes IL-15 throughout development rather than from a formed NK compartment.
Surveillance capacity is read as in vitro lysis of a tumour target cell line and surface phenotype, not as control of transformed or infected cells in tissue.
The rescue uses supraphysiological daily human IL-15, which also expands NK T and CD8 T cells, so it is not a restoration of the endogenous tonic signal.
The authors state that whether IL-15 acts by expanding a residual mature population or by driving precursor maturation was not resolved.
Read in the Europe PMC full text with figure legends; other sections of the paper were read only as far as needed for the NK arm.
studies.observable: Frequency and absolute number of NK1.1+CD3- splenocytes, specific lysis of YAC-1 and P815 targets across effector-to-target ratios, and splenic cellularity
studies.preparation: Splenocytes from naive IL-15-/- and littermate control mice are immunophenotyped for NK1.1 and CD3 and assayed for cytolytic function in an overnight chromium-release assay against NK-sensitive YAC-1 targets, with NK-resistant P815 targets as a specificity control, 24 h after a single injection of PBS or 100 micrograms polyinosinic-polycytidylic acid. For the rescue arm, adult IL-15-/- and control mice are injected intraperitoneally with PBS or 10 micrograms human IL-15 once daily for 7 days and spleens are taken 24 h after the last injection for the same cytolysis and surface-phenotype measurements.

studies.finding: Phenformin and AICAR potently suppressed mTORC1 signalling, including in TSC2−/− MEFs, and mutation of raptor Ser722/Ser792 prevented full suppression in all cell types tested; in TSC2−/− MEFs the AA raptor allele almost fully abolished the suppression and raptor-associated mTORC1 kinase activity was refractory to inhibition. studies.finding: Oxidative and genotoxic stress represses mTORC1 signalling, rapidly (under 60 min) and at low (under 0.1 mM) hydrogen peroxide concentrations, and N-acetylcysteine and catalase rescue the effect; menadione and glutathione depletion repress it as well, and fractionation with leptomycin B places the signalling in the cytoplasm. Autophagy increases concomitantly: GFP-LC3 puncta rise comparably to rapamycin, LC3-II increases, p62 falls over time and autophagosomes appear by electron microscopy. The repression requires an intact cascade: ATM-deficient lymphoblasts do not repress mTORC1, Atm-/- fibroblasts repress significantly less than Atm+/+ and Atm+/- fibroblasts, ATM and LKB1 knockdown attenuate the repression, LKB1-deficient HeLa S3 cells cannot repress and wild-type but not T363A Lkb1 restores it, compound C attenuates it, and Tsc2-/- fibroblasts do not repress although their AMPK is constitutively active, with a TSC2 allele lacking the AMPK sites likewise deficient. At 1 mM hydrogen peroxide and above, repression also proceeds by LKB1-independent routes. The authors state that ATM- and TSC2-independent routes to autophagy have not been ruled out.
studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
limitations: Autophagy is measured as LC3 and p62 markers and autophagosome counts, and the study does not test genetically whether the ROS-induced autophagy requires ATM, TSC2 or mTORC1.
The oxidant is applied pharmacologically, and in several key experiments the cells also lack TSC2 and p53 or are tumour lines.
Senescence outputs of mTOR are not assessed; the supporting figures S1-S7 and the figure images were not read or inspected.
The published correction redefines the error bars of three panels.

Autophagy is followed in parallel as GFP-LC3 puncta after 1 h of hydrogen peroxide, as LC3-II and p62 by immunoblot and as autophagosomes by electron microscopy.

studies.finding: S6K and 4E-BP1 phosphorylation fell within 2 h of starvation and was restored by 6 h and thereafter despite ongoing starvation, as autophagy attenuated and lysosomes reformed from autolysosomes. studies.finding: In proliferating fibroblasts, removing serum and amino acids decreased mTORC1 signalling and raised LC3B-II, whereas in irradiation-, oncogene- and replication-induced senescent cells mTORC1 activity persisted without these signals and LC3B-II did not increase; the source reports that this is specific to senescence rather than quiescence. limitations: Cultured primary human fibroblasts; the quiescence comparison, TSC2 overexpression and Atg5 siRNA data are in supplementary figures that were not read.
